headline: NAB flips to rate cut call and Apple drops a big Siri AI upgrade — a mixed day across the board with everything in the red, but US markets closed higher last night.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG slipped 1.25% last night in a broader NASDAQ tech pullback. No specific Alphabet news drove the move — it was general market rotation. The stock is still up nearly 25% on your cost basis, so this is just noise on a solid position.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI.AX fell 1.22% today, tracking weakness in global AI and tech stocks. Ironically, Apple's big Siri AI announcement and Google/Nvidia partnership news are positive for the sector long-term — this ETF holds those types of companies. Short-term price action doesn't match the headline tailwinds.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT dipped 1.18% last night alongside the broader tech sector softness. No company-specific news drove this — it's a general drift lower for mega-cap tech. Still down about 7% on your total cost, so it's one to watch for a catalyst to turn things around.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG.AX eased 0.8% today, largely reflecting the ASX 200's modest decline and some drag from its US equity exposure (which closed lower last night). Nothing unusual here — this fund moves with global markets.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS.AX slipped another 0.85% today, continuing its rough patch — you're down 13% on this position overall. Lithium stocks across the ASX faced a 'battery reset' with analysts flagging persistent supply pressure. There are some tentative signs of a lithium price revival, but the sector remains under pressure.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO fell 0.86% last night in quiet trade. No major news — the stock is drifting as the market waits for a major game release catalyst. Down about 8.3% on your cost basis overall.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS.AX dropped 0.71% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's slight softness in US large-cap stocks. The ASX-listed price can lag the overnight US session, so this may not fully capture last night's NASDAQ gains yet.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL.AX was almost flat today, slipping just 0.11%. Oil (WTI crude) fell 1.73% last night — dropping about $1.58 to $89.72/barrel — but FUEL.AX barely flinched. Energy stocks held up better than crude itself, which is actually a decent sign of underlying sector resilience.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE.AX was essentially flat today, down just 3 cents. Emerging markets have been quietly stable — no major catalyst either way. Still slightly underwater on your cost basis overall.

watch_today.title: NAB now expects an RBA rate cut — what it means for you
watch_today.detail: NAB has done a major U-turn and now tips the Reserve Bank will cut interest rates, reversing their earlier call for more hikes. This is big news: cheaper borrowing costs tend to boost property prices and growth stocks. Your VDHG, VTS, and GXAI holdings all benefit from a rate-cutting environment. Keep an eye on the RBA's next meeting.

watch_today.name: Global X AI ETF
watch_today.title: Apple's Siri AI overhaul is a tailwind for GXAI.AX
watch_today.detail: Apple today announced a major revamp of Siri and its Apple Intelligence platform, plus a partnership with Google and Nvidia for its most advanced AI model. These are exactly the kinds of companies inside GXAI.AX. The ETF fell 1.22% today but the underlying news is bullish for the sector. Hold — the narrative is strengthening even if price hasn't caught up.

watch_today.name: Pilbara Minerals
watch_today.title: PLS.AX still struggling — lithium sector under pressure
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped another 0.85% today and you're sitting on a 13% loss on this position. ASX lithium stocks are facing a 'battery reset' with analysts citing ongoing supply glut concerns. There are some early signs of a lithium price recovery, but nothing concrete yet. Hold for now — selling at this level locks in the loss, but it's worth reviewing your conviction on a turnaround.

watch_today.name: Microsoft
watch_today.title: MSFT drifting — no catalyst to act on right now
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is down about 7% on your cost basis and has been drifting lower with the rest of big tech. Last night's 1.18% fall was not news-driven. No earnings or major announcements imminent. Hold — but keep an eye on whether AI competition news starts to favour or hurt their Copilot story.

watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil fell $1.58 to $89.72/barrel last night. If oil keeps sliding, FUEL.AX will eventually feel it despite today's near-flat close. Nothing alarming yet, but worth watching if crude breaks below $88.

watch_today.name: Alphabet (Google)
watch_today.title: GOOG still your best performer — sit tight
watch_today.detail: Despite a 1.25% dip last night, GOOG is still up nearly 25% on your cost basis — your strongest position. Apple's new partnership with Google for AI models (announced today) is a genuine positive signal for Alphabet's AI revenue. No reason to move. Hold.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 edged down 0.24% today to close at 8,604 — a quiet session with no dramatic moves. Last night in the US, it was a different story: the NASDAQ jumped 0.86% and the S&P 500 gained 0.3%, with tech leading the charge. Gold hit $4,350/oz, oil slipped 1.73% to $89.72/barrel, and the Aussie dollar ticked slightly higher to 70.51 US cents.

indicators.name: NASDAQ

indicators.name: Gold

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar was nearly flat — slightly stronger on rate cut speculation reducing the US dollar's appeal.

politics.summary: The big story today is NAB flipping its RBA forecast to a rate cut, while the RBA itself is defending its track record. Separately, the NDIS reform bill is getting a hard look in Canberra.

stories.title: NAB tips RBA interest rate cut in major reversal
stories.why_it_matters: NAB has dramatically reversed its earlier call for more rate hikes and now expects the Reserve Bank to cut interest rates. This is a significant shift from one of Australia's biggest banks — it signals that the economic data is softening enough that even the hawkish banks are backing off. For you as an investor, lower rates are generally good news: growth stocks get a boost, mortgages get cheaper, and consumer spending tends to pick up. Watch for the other major banks to follow NAB's lead.

stories.title: RBA defends rate hikes: 'Other countries would kill for our problems'
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA is pushing back against criticism of its rate hike campaign, arguing that Australia's economic resilience — low unemployment, strong growth — is the envy of other countries. The RBA's message: yes, rates went up and it hurt, but we avoided the recession that hit others. This matters because it signals the RBA won't be in a hurry to cut, even as banks like NAB start predicting they will.

stories.title: One of Australia's biggest banks says interest rate pain is over — for now
stories.why_it_matters: A major Australian bank is now saying the rate hiking cycle is done — at least for now. This follows NAB's call for cuts and adds to growing market consensus that the RBA has peaked. For homeowners and borrowers, this is welcome relief. For investors in growth assets (like your portfolio), a rate plateau or eventual cut removes one of the biggest headwinds of the past two years.

stories.title: Six of the most contentious parts of the NDIS bill
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government's NDIS reform bill is working its way through parliament and the ABC has outlined the six most controversial elements — including changes to eligibility criteria, funding caps, and support categories. The NDIS covers about 600,000 Australians with disabilities. The contentious parts mostly revolve around concerns that some participants could lose supports or face increased bureaucratic hurdles. No direct market impact, but it's a significant piece of social policy legislation to follow.

ai.summary: Apple stole the headlines today with a big Siri overhaul and new AI partnerships, while the AI regulation debate heated up on both sides of the Atlantic — with the EU delaying key rules and Trump signing a new executive order that could reshape how US AI labs operate.

stories.title: Apple introduces Siri AI — a 'profoundly more capable and personal assistant'
stories.why_it_matters: Apple officially unveiled the next generation of Siri at WWDC 2026, pitching it as a dramatically smarter, more personal assistant that understands context across your apps and life. This is Apple's biggest AI push yet — moving beyond simple voice commands to a system that can take real actions on your behalf across your iPhone, iPad, and Mac. If it works as advertised, it changes how hundreds of millions of people interact with their devices daily, and puts Apple firmly in the AI assistant race alongside ChatGPT and Google Gemini.

stories.title: Apple partnering with Google and Nvidia for most advanced AI model
stories.why_it_matters: Apple is teaming up with Google and Nvidia to power its most advanced AI model — a significant deal that brings together three of the biggest names in tech. For Google (GOOG, which you hold), this is a major revenue and credibility win: Apple choosing Google's AI infrastructure validates Alphabet's position as a top-tier AI provider. It also means Apple's AI features will be backed by serious horsepower rather than built entirely in-house. Good news for GOOG holders.

stories.title: Trump's new AI order could change how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has signed a new executive order that could significantly change how AI companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic are allowed to release new models in the US. The order is reported to introduce national security and vetting requirements before major AI models can be publicly launched. This adds regulatory uncertainty for AI companies — potentially slowing release timelines — but could also lock in advantages for established players who can navigate compliance more easily. Relevant for your GOOG and GXAI.AX holdings.

stories.title: EU delays key AI rules as Brussels reconsiders pace of regulation
stories.why_it_matters: The European Commission has decided to slow down the rollout of key parts of the EU AI Act — the world's most comprehensive AI regulation framework. Brussels appears to be reconsidering how fast to implement rules, likely in response to concerns that overly aggressive regulation could hurt European competitiveness against the US and China. For global AI companies (including those in your GXAI.AX ETF), a softer EU regulatory timeline is a mild positive — less compliance burden in the near term.

sport.summary: NRL Round 15 team lists are out with Souths copping a brutal blow heading into Thursday's clash. The AFL had a big weekend — Melbourne won a thriller, Collingwood lost a key player, and Gold Coast has a trade domino in the works. Wimbledon season is approaching and the tennis world is watching Sinner.

stories.title: Struggling Souths cop another brutal blow ahead of Round 15 Broncos clash
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney are already struggling in 2026 and have been hit with another injury setback ahead of their Round 15 Thursday night clash against the Brisbane Broncos at Accor Stadium (7:50pm). Coach Jason Demetriou (Madge) has also made a call on his playmaker selection. With Souths in poor form, the Broncos will start strong favourites. The full Round 15 team lists are out now via Sporting News.

stories.title: AFL Roundup: A runaway pair at the top after Hawks and Cats slip up
stories.why_it_matters: Hawthorn and Geelong both dropped games in the AFL weekend, which means the two teams at the top of the ladder are now running away from the pack. Melbourne won a thriller and Collingwood lost a key player — Mihocek was taken to hospital and a Pies star is out — which could reshape the top-eight picture heading into the second half of the season.

stories.title: AFL whispers: Gold Coast trade domino as major update unveiled
stories.why_it_matters: A major trade update is circulating involving the Gold Coast Suns — a trade domino effect that could reshape their list significantly. Details are still emerging but it's shaping up as a notable off-season move for the local Gold Coast club. Worth watching for Suns fans on the Gold Coast.

stories.title: Pressure is off Zverev but Sinner will 'become an even stronger player' — Italian tennis chief
stories.why_it_matters: With Wimbledon approaching, the tennis world is sizing up the big names. Italy's tennis chief says Jannik Sinner will become 'an even stronger player' despite his recent legal battles, while the pressure on Alexander Zverev has eased. Sinner remains the world No.1 and the favourite heading into the grass court season. Wimbledon starts late June.
